sections.title: What actually breaks and what we protect

items.title: Product URLs
items.html: On the iFrame they live on Dutchie’s domain; on Plus they disappear if the storefront goes offline. We map indexed URLs by priority and send every changed URL to its closest equivalent with a 301 redirect.

items.title: Menu Crawlability
items.html: iFrame menus are effectively uncrawlable. Dutchie Pro renders store and product pages Googlebot can actually read and index.

items.title: Product Schema
items.html: Product structured data should come from live menu data, not hardcoded markup. We validate and optimize it where Dutchie’s data and Google’s rules support it.

items.title: Core Web Vitals
items.html: On the iFrame your speed is tied to Dutchie’s render budget. On Pro, page performance is back under your control.

items.title: Internal Links
items.html: Links from blog posts and local pages must resolve to indexable pages, not a frame or a 404. We verify every one post-cutover.

items.title: AI Citability
items.html: Assistants can’t cite a menu that isn’t really on your domain. Indexable product pages are the precondition for AI search visibility.

sections.title: Proof, not theory: Verdi Cannabis and Mighty Lucky

blocks.html: Verdi Cannabis ran its menu on the default Dutchie iFrame, with every product page invisible to Google. We migrated the menu to Dutchie Pro, preserved the existing URL and link structure, put 301 redirects in place for anything that had to change, and rebuilt their blog and podcast templates on WordPress. Comparing the six months after migration to the six before: organic impressions grew +93.5%, organic clicks +17%, and average position climbed +7 spots, from the bottom of page 2 to the top of page 1. Seven of the top ten traffic pages had little to no visibility before the move. The site went from ranking almost entirely for its own brand name to holding page-1 positions for non-branded, high-intent terms like “dispensary near me” and “park slope dispensary”: exactly the neighborhood demand that used to go to competitors.

items.label: Read the Full Verdi Case Study

blocks.html: Mighty Lucky on the Bowery in Lower Manhattan is a different kind of project: a custom Dutchie Pro storefront built with the Dutchie Pro SDK. We built a custom theme and branded navigation, served the store on the dispensary’s own domain through a Cloudflare reverse proxy, integrated it with their Shopify site, and shipped 301 redirects and a sitemap for the new store. The store is still in its post-launch monitoring period, so this case shows the technical build, not ranking results yet.

We’ve carried a licensed NYC dispensary from an invisible iFrame menu to page-1 rankings, and we can show the Search Console proof. Migration is a technical, local, and content problem at once, and we handle all three.

We work directly with Dutchie as a certified partner. That gives our clients a direct line to the Dutchie team during migration, and one agency that handles the platform, the SEO, and the content.

sections.title: We migrate dispensaries specifically, not as a side service.

blocks.html: A cannabis migration isn’t a generic rebuild. The compliance rules, the platform quirks, and the SEO stakes are different, and getting them wrong during a cutover is how listings get suspended at the worst possible moment. Here’s what a clean Dutchie Pro migration includes:

items: Priority-based URL mapping. Indexed URLs are crawled and ranked by traffic and links before anything is touched, and each changed URL is mapped to its closest equivalent: product, category, or a relevant fallback page.
301 redirects for every changed URL. Ranking pages and internal links don’t land on a 404.
Product structured data. Generated from live menu data, validated and optimized where Dutchie’s data and Google’s rules support it.
30/60/90-day monitoring. Indexation diffs against baseline, with any page that slips diagnosed and fixed.

sections.title: A migration is your entry ticket to AI search.

blocks.html: When someone asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google’s AI for a dispensary recommendation, it names a handful, built on clear, crawlable, trustworthy pages. An iFrame menu is invisible to them for the same reason it’s invisible to Googlebot. A Dutchie Pro migration is the precondition for GEO / AI search visibility: you can’t be the assistant’s pick for “Brooklyn dispensary with X in stock” if your inventory pages don’t exist as real, structured URLs.
Most dispensaries have zero presence here today. Migrate cleanly now and you get to own the AI recommendation before competitors realize it’s a channel.

sections.title: How we run a Dutchie Pro migration

items.title: Baseline Audit & URL Mapping
items.html: We crawl the current setup and export every indexed URL, ranking position, and internal-link count. This becomes the recovery target and the priority map for redirects to Dutchie Pro.

items.title: Migration & Redirects
items.html: We migrate the live menu to Dutchie Pro with the URL structure preserved, put 301 redirects in place for anything that changes, and set up product structured data where supported and a new XML sitemap.

items.title: Verification
items.html: We re-crawl the new structure, validate schema in Rich Results Test, confirm indexing in Search Console, and test every redirect end to end before calling the cutover done.

items.title: 30/60/90-Day Monitoring
items.html: Migrations aren’t finished at go-live. We run indexation diffs against baseline, watch Core Web Vitals and rankings, and remediate any URL that slips.

sections.title: Which path is right for your dispensary?

blocks.html: There are three honest responses to a legacy Plus storefront or an unindexed iFrame. Falling back to the standard iFrame is cheapest but throws away product URLs and schema, so it’s only sensible for a low-volume store that never indexed products. Switching providers (Jane, Treez, Flowhub) is a 60–90 day project that only makes sense if you were already leaving Dutchie. For everyone else with traffic to protect or earn, migrating to Dutchie E-Commerce Pro is the default: you keep your POS, staff, and customer accounts and gain indexable pages plus a foundation for local and AI search. Not sure which applies? Run site:yourdomain.com inurl:/products/ in Google, then get a free audit.

faq.title: Dutchie Pro migration FAQ

items.q: Are you an official Dutchie partner?
items.a: Yes. Tarasovs Agency is a {{PARTNER_STATUS}} under a signed partner agreement with Dutchie. We are an independent agency and build Dutchie Pro storefronts for licensed dispensaries.

items.q: When is Dutchie Plus being sunset?
items.a:
Dutchie has said it will support legacy Dutchie Plus customers through the end of 2026. Exact end-of-life dates are tier-dependent, so request a written timeline from your Dutchie account manager and plan to complete migration well before the API stops responding.

We checked Dutchie's own Help Center, release notes, and product pages before publishing this, and none of them list a public cutoff date or deprecation schedule. The end-of-2026 date and any specific timeline you see quoted elsewhere comes from account-level communication, not a published company announcement. Treat it as unconfirmed until your account manager puts a date in writing.

items.q: What's the difference between the Dutchie iFrame and Dutchie Pro?
items.a: The default iFrame embeds your menu from Dutchie's domain inside a frame, which search engines struggle to index as real pages. Dutchie Pro serves store and product pages as standalone, crawlable URLs on your own domain, so each can be found, ranked, and cited individually.

items.q: Can you build a custom Dutchie Pro storefront, not just migrate?
items.a: Yes. We work with the Dutchie E-Commerce Pro SDK to build custom themes, branded navigation, product and category layouts, and integrations with Shopify or WordPress, served on your own domain through Cloudflare. Mighty Lucky on the Bowery is a live example.

items.q: Will migrating to Dutchie Pro hurt my SEO?
items.a: Only if it's done without proper URL mapping and redirects. The real risks are URL changes without 301s, dropped metadata, broken internal links, and stale schema. We map indexed URLs by priority before migration and preserve structure wherever possible. That’s why Verdi's rankings grew through the migration instead of dropping.

items.q: How long does a Dutchie Pro migration take to show results?
items.a: Indexing of newly crawlable pages typically begins within the first few weeks. Meaningful ranking and traffic gains build over 3–6 months as Google gains confidence in the new URLs, consistent with the six-month window behind the Verdi results.

items.q: Do I have to leave Dutchie to fix my menu SEO?
items.a: No. If you're happy with Dutchie operationally, migrating to Dutchie Pro keeps your POS, staff, and customer accounts while making your menu indexable. Switching providers only makes sense if you were already planning to leave for other reasons.

items.q: Can you migrate a multi-location / MSO setup?
items.a: Yes. Multi-location migrations need more URL mapping and per-location QA, and we scope the timeline accordingly. Store-location pages are usually among the biggest winners, since each becomes an indexable, locally relevant page instead of a menu tab.

items.q: What does a Dutchie Pro migration cost?
items.a: Engagements are scoped to your setup: how many URLs are indexed, whether you're on Plus or the iFrame, and how much local and content work you want alongside the technical migration. The honest starting point is the free audit; it shows what's actually needed before you commit.
